verdict: AMD's revenue leapt 50% to a record $11.5B as data-center sales more than doubled — and this time the growth reached the bottom line, with net profit nearly tripling to $2.3B.

segments.name: Data Center
segments.note: EPYC server processors and Instinct AI accelerators — more than doubled as AI data centers kept buying; the segment earned $2.1B of operating profit vs a loss a year ago.

segments.name: Client
segments.note: Ryzen processors for PCs — up 23% as the PC market and AI PCs grew.

segments.name: Gaming
segments.note: Graphics cards and console chips — down 31%, mostly weaker semi-custom console business.

segments.name: Embedded
segments.note: Chips built into cars, industrial gear and communications equipment (the Xilinx business).

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next generations of CPUs, GPUs and AI accelerators — up 33% YoY.

opex.name: Marketing, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling products and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization of acquisition intangibles
opex.note: Writing down the value of technology bought in acquisitions (Xilinx above all) — a bookkeeping charge, not cash.

takeaways.title: Data Center is now the company
takeaways.text: Data Center revenue more than doubled to $6.7B — 58% of everything AMD sells — and its operating profit swung from a $155M loss a year ago to $2.1B.

takeaways.title: Gaming is shrinking
takeaways.text: Gaming revenue fell 31% to $779M as console-chip demand faded — the old business is shrinking while the AI business replaces it.

takeaways.title: Capex nearly tripled
takeaways.text: Spending on property and equipment jumped from $282M to $808M as AMD builds out capacity for AI demand; free cash flow still rose to $1.6B.

oneTimers: Other income includes $483M of net gains on long-term investments (per the cash-flow statement) — paper gains, not cash from selling chips.
An $8M loss from discontinued operations sits below the continuing-operations line; profit from continuing operations was $2,305M.
otherDetail: Other income of $598M (mostly gains on long-term investments) plus $6M of equity income, less $37M of interest expense and an $8M loss from discontinued operations — a net +$559M.
follow100Note: The rows reconcile to $100 within a cent or two of rounding.
